title: A Landfall for the Horizon
premise: Desert ranger Rosalind Marchetti follows a thief into the flooded lowlands, only to find a vanished government survey team whose gear sits abandoned with no tracks leading away. Teaming up with the thief himself—Ezra Voss, who stole her compass because it hides a map to a buried reservoir—she discovers the surveyors were silenced to conceal a dam project that will drown three villages. As the monsoon closes in and their boat takes on water, Rosalind must choose between exposing the truth that will cost her the ranger's badge she's clung to since her father's disgrace, or staying loyal to the service that made her belong somewhere. She chooses truth, riding out the flood in the reservoir's old spillway, and emerges to testify—losing her post but gaining a community, and finally understanding what her father was trying to tell her all along.
about_author: Dominic Hartwell is a former hydrological surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote river basins before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember more than the people who cross them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Nothing
chapters.summary: Rosalind tracks a thief across the empty salt flats, rationing water and memory in alternating flashes of her father's disgrace. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: lonely determination; she catches Ezra Voss at dusk and demands her compass back.

chapters.title: What the Compass Hides
chapters.summary: Ezra refuses to surrender the compass, revealing a hidden etching beneath its face—a map fragment. He claims he stole it from the survey team, not her. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into reluctant curiosity as she realizes her father owned this compass first.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: They reach the survey camp: tents pitched, instruments running, food rotting, no bodies, no tracks. Rosalind reads the ground like scripture and finds nothing—which frightens her more than blood would. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: professional confidence cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The Radio That Answers
chapters.summary: The camp radio crackles with an official order to stand down and return to the capital. Ezra says the voice is wrong—the survey chief never spoke like that. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: his streetwise cynicism meets her institutional trust, and both begin to waver.

chapters.title: Downstream of Silence
chapters.summary: Following the map fragment downstream, they find the first drowned village—already flooded by 'test releases.' A survivor, old Marta, recognizes the compass and calls it 'the key your father buried.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief and vertigo; her family history is tangled in this crime.

chapters.title: A Debt in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Ezra confesses his motive: his brother was one of the vanished surveyors, and he stole the compass to find him. Rosalind realizes their debts run parallel. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: guarded confession forging fragile alliance over a shared fire.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Clouds stack on the horizon. They reach the river depot and find one boat—leaking, undersupplied—and a government notice declaring the valley closed for 'flood management.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency; the land itself becomes hostile.

chapters.title: The Man from the Ministry
chapters.summary: Ministry agent Corliss intercepts them, offering Rosalind reinstatement if she surrenders the compass and forgets the valley. Her loyalty to the service wars with everything she's seen. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: temptation delivered politely; she refuses, and becomes a fugitive.

chapters.title: Running the Narrows
chapters.summary: Pursued by Corliss's patrol boat, they shoot the river narrows in the storm's first rain. Ezra's river knowledge saves them; Rosalind's seamanship saves the boat. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: adrenaline-bonded trust—they stop being strangers.

chapters.title: The Second Village
chapters.summary: They warn the village of Kel Anoor; some flee, some refuse to believe. Rosalind sees belonging from the outside—people rooted where she has never been rooted. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: envy and tenderness; she wants what they have.

chapters.title: Bailing by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Storm-bound in a boathouse, they repair the hull and decode more of the compass map: the reservoir's original spillway, built by their grandparents' generation, deliberately misdocumented. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy in confinement; Rosalind tells Ezra the full story of her father's ruin.

chapters.title: What Her Father Knew
chapters.summary: A hidden letter in the compass case reveals her father surveyed this valley thirty years ago and was destroyed for reporting the spillway's existence. His 'disgrace' was silencing. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: devastating reframe—her whole identity was built on a lie.

chapters.title: Corliss Closes In
chapters.summary: Patrols sweep the valley. A betrayed villager sells their location; they escape through cane fields as flares light the sky. Marta is taken for questioning. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: guilt and fury—their presence endangers everyone who helps them.

chapters.title: The Vanished Found
chapters.summary: In an abandoned mine shaft marked on the compass map, they find the survey team alive but imprisoned—starving witnesses held until after the flooding. Among them, Ezra's brother, barely conscious. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into resolve; now they must move six broken people.

chapters.title: Six Souls, One Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: The evacuation downriver in rising water: bailing in shifts, rations halved, Corliss's searchlights behind them. The survey chief confirms the dam will fail catastrophically, not just drown villages. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: exhausted solidarity; leadership passes between them naturally now.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: One rescued surveyor, terrified for his pension, radios Corliss. Ambush at the old weir; Ezra is captured covering the others' escape. Rosalind must choose: rescue him or deliver the evidence to the capital. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made flesh—she cannot do both.

chapters.title: Into the Spillway
chapters.summary: Rosalind leads the survivors into the ancient spillway as the monsoon peaks, trusting her father's map over the ministry's charts. Inside: dry stone, old tools, and proof her father planned this refuge decades ago. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: communion with the dead; she finally feels her father beside her.

chapters.title: The Flood Comes
chapters.summary: The engineered release begins early. From inside the spillway they watch the valley drown through the grate—Kel Anoor's rooftops vanishing, the evidence of the crime literally submerged. POV: Ezra. Emotional beat: helpless witness; grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Corliss's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rosalind goes back for Ezra alone, trading herself to Corliss in exchange—but the imprisoned villagers' testimony and the survey chief's records arrive via radio to the capital before Corliss can bury them. His own superiors turn. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewarded not by luck but by the web of people she chose to trust.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Dry Season
chapters.summary: Weeks later: hearings in the capital. Rosalind testifies, resigning her commission rather than let the service launder her words. Ezra's brother recovers; the villages are compensated; the dam project collapses. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: costly vindication—truth won, belonging redefined.

chapters.title: The Compass Returned
chapters.summary: Rosalind returns to the valley, now a protected watershed. Marta gives her back the compass; she leaves it, open, on her father's old survey marker. Belonging, she understands, is something you build, not something you're issued. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: quiet release of inherited shame.

chapters.title: A Landfall for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Rosalind and Ezra launch a small survey outfit of their own, mapping forgotten waterways for the communities who live on them. On the horizon, storm clouds gather again—but this time there are people waiting to be warned. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: hopeful forward motion; the adventure continues, no longer alone.
